description:
In this position... 
 The Battery Management Embedded Software Engineer owns the base software platform beneath the application layer for high-voltage battery management controllers — the real-time operating system, hardware abstraction, drivers, communication stacks, software update mechanism, and security foundation.
 Assignments may include string-level or system-level battery management controllers and may shift across the product architecture over the life of the program.
 The ideal candidate has brought up embedded hardware from first power-on, written drivers from datasheets, integrated and hardened communication stacks, and owned a production software update path.

 What you'll do...
 Own board bring-up and hardware abstraction: clocks, memory, timers, interrupts, watchdog, and system basis chip integration.
 Configure and maintain the real-time operating system and scheduling architecture; own task partitioning, timing budgets, and runtime monitoring.
 Develop and integrate device drivers for cell monitoring front-end devices, voltage and current measurement, isolation monitoring interfaces, analog and digital I/O, high-side drivers, discrete inputs and outputs, and non-volatile storage.
 Own communication stacks and services, including automotive serial networks and diagnostic services.
 Own the bootloader and the software flashing, update, and rollback mechanism, including update across multiple controllers.
 Implement secure boot, secure flashing, secure debug access, signed image verification, and hardware security module key handling, in partnership with cybersecurity engineering.
 Own persistent data logging and event storage, including storage media management, retention, and retrieval.
 Own the embedded build environment, static analysis, unit test framework, and continuous integration pipeline.
 Integrate application, controls, and algorithm software onto the platform; support application engineers with debug, tracing, and runtime measurement.
 Define and document the base-software-to-application interface so application development can proceed independently of the platform.
 Support supplier software assessment and technical transfer.
 Debug at the hardware level with oscilloscopes, logic and protocol analyzers, and on-chip debuggers.
 
 You'll have...
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
 5+ years developing embedded software in C for resource-constrained real-time systems.
 Strong microcontroller architecture fundamentals: memory maps, interrupts, DMA, timing, and determinism.
 Production experience with a real-time operating system or equivalent scheduling framework.
 Driver development from datasheets and hands-on hardware debug experience.
 Communication protocol implementation experience including CAN or CAN FD.
 Bootloader, flashing, or software update implementation experience.
 Version control, code review, and continuous integration discipline.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 Ability and willingness to travel occasionally
  
 Even better, you may have...
 Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Science.
 Battery management, high-voltage, or safety-relevant control unit software experience.
 Layered automotive base software architecture experience.
 Experience interfacing to cell monitoring front-end devices over isolated serial or CAN-based interfaces.
 Secure boot, secure flashing, hardware security module, or cryptographic library integration.
 Software development under functional safety and cybersecurity process requirements.
 Familiarity with industrial communication protocol stacks in addition to automotive networks.
 MISRA C compliance and static analysis toolchains.
 Continuous integration and hardware-in-the-loop automation for embedded targets.
 Technical Skills Embedded C for real-time systems
 Real-time operating system configuration and scheduling
 Hardware abstraction and driver development
 Board bring-up and hardware debug
 Communication stacks and diagnostic services
 Bootloader, flashing, update, and rollback
 Secure boot, secure flashing, and key handling
 Non-volatile storage and data logging
 Build environment, static analysis, and continuous integration
 Base software to application interface definition
 Timing analysis and runtime measurement
 
  
 You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!
 As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:
• Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage
• Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up child care and more
• Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more
• Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases
• Tuition assistance
• Established and active employee resource groups
• Paid time off for individual and team community service 
• A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day 
• Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time. 
 
 This position is a salary grade 7 and ranges from $99,600-$166,600., 
 This position is a salary grade 8 and ranges from $115,000-$192,900.     
 Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.
